We are a team of secondary school students interested in science and new knowledge; we get excited about new discoveries and take on new challenges with the firm belief that knowledge is meant to be shared.

Somos un equipo de jovenes de secundaria, interesados en las ciencias y los nuevos conocimientos, nos emocionan los nuevos descubrimientos y asumimos los nuevos retos con la firme idea que el conocimiento es para compartirlo.
summary: We designed an interactive simulator using Python and Pygame that allows children aged 7 to 14 to manage a space base on the Moon or Mars. transforms space education into a hands-on experience
details:
Cygnus Squad Simulator: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational simulation game designed for children ages 7 to 14. Players take the role of mission commanders responsible for managing a lunar or Martian habitat.

The simulator challenges players to balance critical systems such as oxygen production, power generation, communications, scientific research, food production, and habitat maintenance. During gameplay, users must make decisions under pressure, respond to emergencies, and complete exploration missions while keeping their crew safe.

Players can choose between a Moon or Mars mission, interact with virtual assistants and non-player characters, explore the environment, collect scientific information, and solve real-world inspired challenges based on space exploration scenarios.

The project makes space science more accessible and engaging for young learners through experiential learning. Instead of passively reading about space exploration, students actively solve problems and experience the consequences of their decisions.

The simulator develops critical thinking, resource management, problem-solving, teamwork, scientific reasoning, and decision-making skills. It also increases interest in STEM education by allowing students to experience the challenges astronauts and mission engineers face during exploration missions.

By combining education and gameplay, the project encourages curiosity and long-term interest in science and space technologies.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, astronauts, and innovators by transforming space education into an immersive experience.

We aim to help children understand how complex systems work together to sustain life beyond Earth while developing practical problem-solving skills. The project seeks to bridge the gap between theoretical learning and hands-on experience, allowing students to apply scientific concepts in realistic scenarios.

Ultimately, we want students to think like space explorers, understand the importance of science and technology, and become active participants in solving future global challenges.

The project was developed using Python as the primary programming language and Pygame as the game development framework.

Our team utilized several artificial intelligence tools to accelerate development, including Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude Code, and Google Gemini. These tools supported software design, coding assistance, debugging, and content generation.

We also researched NASA resources and datasets, including:

• NASA Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI) • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) • NASA Trek Mars

Development was carried out on standard personal computers capable of supporting Python development, graphics rendering, and game testing.

Our project combines educational gaming, space exploration, interactive storytelling, simulation mechanics, and real NASA-inspired concepts into a single learning experience.

Unlike traditional educational materials, students do not simply receive information. They become mission commanders responsible for making decisions that directly affect the survival and success of a lunar or Martian colony.

The combination of resource management, environmental hazards, scientific missions, virtual assistants, character interaction, and exploration creates a unique and engaging approach to STEM learning that transforms complex scientific concepts into interactive challenges.

During development, our team focused on several key factors:

• Educational value and alignment with STEM learning objectives.

• Age-appropriate gameplay for children between 7 and 14 years old.

• Accessibility and ease of use for students with different experience levels.

• Scientific accuracy inspired by real space exploration challenges.

• Engagement through missions, exploration, characters, and interactive decision-making.

• Scalability to allow future integration of additional NASA datasets and missions.

• Balance between entertainment and meaningful learning outcomes.

• User experience, ensuring that players can learn while having fun.

We also considered how to transform real-world challenges faced by astronauts into simplified but realistic gameplay mechanics that children can understand and enjoy.
